newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand was a touch weaker in moribund dealings late on Monday, dampened by a public holiday in the U.K and a strong and stable dollar.
Bonds had an equally uninspiring day, trapped in narrow ranges, searching for direction amid an absence of local economic data reports.
At 1400 GMT the rand was trading at 4.4550/4580 on the dollar from 4.4510/4540 late on Friday after holding in tight 4.4510-4560 bid band on day.
"It's been extremely quiet with the London guys mostly away," a trader said.
"The factors causing the slight weakening were the continued strong dollar and some importer demand coupled with the lack of offshore dollar sales."
Traders said London banks had been big sellers of dollars in recent months.
They said a close above the 4.45 level was technically bearish and pointed to further weakness in the near term.
"It could cause the rand to drift up to the 4.47-4750 level this week," one trader said.
Tuesday's trade was seen duplicating Monday's lethargy with the rand tracking higher to open around 4.4570-4580 and edging above the 4.46 level during the day.
Dealers said the Reserve Bank was unlikely to intervene at these levels. "But if the 4.47-4.750 comes into view, the Bank may be interested," a dealer said.
Against the crosses, the rand was last at 7.2143/2218 on sterling from 7.1915/2008 late on Friday, having shed most of the gains it made against sterling last week.
Against the mark, the rand was last quoted at 0.3883/3887 from 0.3881/3885, and was at 28.4167/4470 yen from 28.4351/4655 yen previously.
On the bond market the key R150 was at 14.825 percent from 14.80 late Friday, after clinging to the centre of day's 14.77-14.875 trading range for most of the afternoon.
Dealers said institutions had been scarce, although one trader said there was small bits of demand at the 14.86 percent level.
The drift up in yields was blamed on jobbers being caught long after Friday's options close-out.
During the day bonds shrugged off better-than-expected gold and foreign exchange reserves data, released on Friday, and a slight weakness on the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond on Monday afternoon.
Dealings were seen continuing dull on Tuesday unless London players, after being absent on Monday, were active in the market. Bonds were seen hugging their recent 14.75-85 percent range.
"There are no (economic) figures this week...about the only thing that will drive this market is if there are some new Eurorand issues," one dealer said.

The Bond Exchange said foreigners were net sellers of 220.19 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Friday, the first net sales position in several weeks, after buying 164.26 million rand's worth on Wednesday. Thursday was a public holiday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 43.69 billion rand from 11.03 billion rand previously.
Major banks kept their three month deposit rates steady at between 16.40 to 16.45 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at between 15.80 to 15.95 percent.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage dipped to 9.048 billion rand on Saturday from 9.070 billion on Friday.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
